brief: The town grows food, sells it, and the food evaporates. produce[] fills from the plots per cell (plotTal, #159); stockMarket() turns the day's stock into mkShelf/mkBoards and computes `sold`; MK_KEEP 0.5 of the surplus stores to the next market and the remainder is simply dropped. Nothing downstream reads `sold`. Meanwhile CAFE_TABLES serves a cup and a saucer with no supply at all, and mkLine() is the only place the town ever says what it sold. PRICE THIS FIRST — grep `sold`, mkShelf, mkGoods(, produce[ and the cafe, because I read the source and not the running town, and there may be a consumer I missed; if there is, say so and re-aim at whatever the grep shows is genuinely unconnected. Otherwise: give the market's output a destination a viewer can SEE from the wide shot on a market afternoon, and one that is visibly absent on a bare February market when mkTotal is 0.
successLooksLike: On a market afternoon something in the frame is legibly the market's doing and is not the stalls; on a February market with mkTotal 0 the same thing is absent. Quote the two states over a swept year, not one screenshot each.
avoid: Do not add a fourth stall — MK_NEED is measured off 120 markets and says one stall on 24% of them already, so the pitches are under-used before you add one. Do not add a second text surface: the town has exactly ONE line of prose and it stays one line. If the honest answer after pricing is a 40-line change, ship 40 lines and say why.
